section_title: Brent-Dubai EFS Arbitrage, WTI Netbacks & China Port Inventory Days of Melt
section_path_text: Commodity Arbitrage > Crude & Ore Stocks > EFS & Inventory Days
text: Energy & bulk arbitrage indicators: Brent-Dubai Exchange of Futures for Swaps (EFS) stands at .85/bbl, while WTI Houston crude trades at a -.40/bbl discount to landed Brent CFR Asia. This keeps the Atlantic-to-Asia crude export arbitrage open for US Gulf (LOOP/Corpus Christi) and Brazilian crude, directly underpinning VLCC TD22 and TD3C tonne-mile employment. On dry bulk, China total imported iron ore port stocks stand at 157.0 Mt across 45 major ports (up 19.7% YoY). Dividing total port inventory by current daily blast furnace hot metal output (2.38 Mt/day) gives 39.2 days of consumption (74.5th percentile). The comfortable inventory cushion explains why steel mills buy hand-to-mouth, moderating aggressive prompt spot ore bids despite high absolute freight.
